topic: Atomic Store with Memory Ordering in C++
explanation: In modern C++, atomic operations are used to perform thread-safe modifications of shared data without data races. The 'atomic_store_explicit' function allows storing a value into an atomic object with a specified memory order, controlling how memory operations are synchronized across threads. This is essential for writing correct concurrent programs, ensuring visibility and ordering guarantees as per the C++ memory model.
syntax: void atomic_store_explicit(std::shared_ptr<T>* p, std::shared_ptr<T> r, std::memory_order mo);
example_explanation: This example demonstrates the use of 'atomic_store_explicit' to store a shared pointer into an atomic variable with a specific memory order (release). It ensures that prior writes are visible to other threads that perform a corresponding load with 'memory_order_acquire'. The code shows how to perform thread-safe, ordered storage of shared pointers, illustrating the concept of explicit atomic operations with memory ordering in C++ concurrency.
